interviewGuide.title: Interview Guide
interviewGuide.description: Behavioral interview questions for {count} competency gaps
interviewGuide.starNote: Use STAR format: ask about a Situation, Task, Action, and Result.

leadership.q1: Describe a time when you had to lead a team through a challenging project. What was your approach, and what was the outcome?
leadership.q2: Tell me about a situation where you had to make a difficult decision that affected your team. How did you handle it?
leadership.q3: Give an example of when you mentored or developed someone on your team. What strategies did you use?

communication.q1: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex idea to someone without technical background. How did you ensure they understood?
communication.q2: Describe a situation where miscommunication led to a problem. How did you resolve it?
communication.q3: Give an example of when you had to deliver difficult feedback. How did you approach the conversation?

problem_solving.q1: Describe a complex problem you encountered at work. Walk me through your problem-solving process.
problem_solving.q2: Tell me about a time you had to make a decision with incomplete information. What was your approach?
problem_solving.q3: Give an example of when your initial solution to a problem did not work. How did you adapt?

teamwork.q1: Tell me about a time you worked with a difficult team member. How did you handle the situation?
teamwork.q2: Describe a project where collaboration was essential to success. What role did you play?
teamwork.q3: Give an example of when you had to resolve a conflict between team members. What was the outcome?

adaptability.q1: Describe a time when priorities changed suddenly. How did you adjust your approach?
adaptability.q2: Tell me about a situation where you had to learn something new quickly to complete a task. How did you approach it?
adaptability.q3: Give an example of when you faced significant uncertainty. How did you maintain effectiveness?

technical.q1: Describe a challenging technical problem you solved. What tools or methods did you use?
technical.q2: Tell me about a time you had to quickly learn a new technology. How did you get up to speed?
technical.q3: Give an example of when you improved a technical process or system. What was the impact?

planning.q1: Describe how you organized a complex project with multiple deadlines. What was your planning process?
planning.q2: Tell me about a time when your plan did not go as expected. How did you adjust?
planning.q3: Give an example of how you prioritize tasks when everything seems urgent.

creativity.q1: Tell me about an innovative solution you proposed at work. What inspired it?
creativity.q2: Describe a time when you had to think outside the box to solve a problem.
creativity.q3: Give an example of when you challenged the status quo. What was the result?

ethics.q1: Describe a situation where you faced an ethical dilemma at work. How did you handle it?
ethics.q2: Tell me about a time you had to stand up for what was right, even when it was unpopular.
ethics.q3: Give an example of how you maintain accountability and integrity in your work.

customer_focus.q1: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer or client. What did you do?
customer_focus.q2: Describe a situation where you had to balance customer needs with business constraints.
customer_focus.q3: Give an example of when you turned a negative customer experience into a positive one.

general.q1: Describe a recent accomplishment you are proud of in this competency area. What made it successful?
general.q2: Tell me about a time you received constructive feedback in this area. How did you respond?
general.q3: Give an example of how you have developed this skill over time. What steps did you take?

onboarding.title: Onboarding Recommendations
onboarding.description: Actionable onboarding guidance based on team dynamics analysis

collaborative.label: Collaborative Communicator
collaborative.description: Naturally engages others and builds consensus. Thrives in open discussion and group brainstorming. Pair with structured check-ins to maintain focus.

assertive.label: Assertive Communicator
assertive.description: Direct and action-oriented. Communicates clearly and decisively. May benefit from active listening exercises during onboarding.

analytical.label: Analytical Communicator
analytical.description: Prefers data-driven discussion and well-structured communication. Give advance notice of meetings with clear agendas.

reflective.label: Reflective Communicator
reflective.description: Thoughtful and deliberate. Prefers written communication and time to process. Provide written summaries of key discussions.

creative.label: Creative Communicator
creative.description: Open to ideas and enjoys brainstorming. Encourage idea-sharing sessions and provide creative problem-solving opportunities.

structured.label: Structured Communicator
structured.description: Values clarity, consistency, and process. Provide clear documentation and well-defined communication channels.

balanced.label: Balanced Communicator
balanced.description: Adaptable communication style. Can adjust to different team dynamics and situations.

specialist.label: Domain Specialist
specialist.description: Deep expertise in specific areas. Leverage their knowledge for mentoring and technical guidance in their strength areas.

leader.label: Natural Leader
leader.description: High capability across multiple areas. Consider early project leadership or initiative ownership opportunities.

gapFiller.label: Gap Filler
gapFiller.description: Brings skills the team currently lacks. Prioritize tasks that leverage their unique contributions to team diversity.

collaborator.label: Team Collaborator
collaborator.description: Balanced skills with strong interpersonal ability. Ideal for cross-functional tasks and bridge-building between sub-teams.

generalist.label: Versatile Generalist
generalist.description: Consistent performance across all areas. Effective in utility roles and can support multiple workstreams.

contributor.label: Developing Contributor
contributor.description: Building foundational skills. Pair with experienced team members for structured learning opportunities.

teamIntegration.title: Team Integration Sessions
teamIntegration.description: Schedule informal 1-on-1s with each team member in the first two weeks. Focus on understanding team workflows and communication norms.

leverageStrengths.title: Leverage Communication Strengths
leverageStrengths.description: Assign early presentations or facilitation roles to help establish credibility and build team rapport quickly.

gradualExposure.title: Gradual Team Exposure
gradualExposure.description: Start with smaller group interactions before full-team settings. Provide written materials ahead of meetings for preparation.

buildRelationships.title: Relationship Building
buildRelationships.description: Create opportunities for informal interaction such as pair programming, lunch meetings, or collaborative side projects.

skillDevelopment.title: Targeted Skill Development
skillDevelopment.description: Identify 1-2 key competency gaps and create a 30-60-90 day development plan with specific learning objectives and mentor support.

differentiateRole.title: Role Differentiation
differentiateRole.description: Clarify distinct responsibilities early to avoid overlap with existing team members. Focus on areas where they add unique value.

mentorship.title: Buddy/Mentor Assignment
mentorship.description: Pair with an experienced team member who can provide context, answer questions, and facilitate knowledge transfer.

recommendations.stronglyRecommend: Strongly recommend for the position. The candidate demonstrates exceptional competency across all key areas with significant strengths that exceed requirements.
recommendations.recommend: Recommend for the position. The candidate meets the benchmark requirements and shows solid competency across assessed areas.
recommendations.conditionalConsider: Consider with conditions. The candidate shows promise but has notable gaps that should be addressed through targeted development or further evaluation.
recommendations.notRecommend: Not recommended at this time. The candidate has significant competency gaps that require substantial development before meeting position requirements.
recommendations.strongProfile: Strong competency profile. The candidate demonstrates advanced proficiency across assessed areas with clear signature strengths.
recommendations.moderateProfile: Moderate competency profile. The candidate shows solid foundational skills with identified areas for continued professional development.
recommendations.developingProfile: Developing competency profile. The candidate is building foundational skills and would benefit from structured development opportunities.
